checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are P2P messages containing transactions validated independently of peer reputation?

reachability.notes: An attacker compromises a previously well-behaved peer and begins sending invalid transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the P2P message handling code for transaction reception (tb-002 boundary). 2. Establish a peer connection and send multiple valid transactions to build trust/history. 3. After establishing trust, send a transaction with gasLimit > 16777216. 4. Verify the transaction is rejected with appropriate error code. 5. Confirm no cached validation results from the peer are used to bypass local validation. 6. Check that the rejection occurs at the P2P message handling layer or transaction pool validation layer. 7. Verify the peer is not automatically trusted based on previous successful transactions.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0046, Trust Boundaries: tb-002, tb-009, Primary Element: SG-001, Source Assumption: asm-009, Source Threat: stride-002

checklist.title: Verify no peer reputation caching bypasses transaction validation for gasLimit checks

reachability.notes: An attacker compromises a previously well-behaved peer and begins sending invalid transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the txpool validation logic (actor-txpool) for any peer reputation-based shortcuts. 2. Search for any caching mechanisms that store validation results keyed by peer ID. 3. Check if there are any code paths where transactions from 'trusted' peers skip validation. 4. Verify that gasLimit validation (> 16777216 rejection) is performed unconditionally. 5. Test by sending transactions from the same peer in rapid succession with alternating valid/invalid gasLimits. 6. Confirm each transaction is validated independently regardless of prior validation outcomes.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0046, Supporting check for peer reputation bypass vectors, Covers: actor-p2p-peer to actor-txpool flow

checklist.title: Verify block validation is independent of peer history at trust boundary tb-009

reachability.notes: An attacker compromises a previously well-behaved peer and begins sending invalid transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the P2P block reception handler at trust boundary tb-009. 2. Establish a peer that has successfully propagated valid blocks. 3. Send a block containing a transaction with gasLimit > 16777216. 4. Verify the block is rejected during validation, not accepted due to peer history. 5. Check that block validation does not short-circuit based on peer reputation. 6. Confirm that each block's transactions are fully re-validated locally regardless of source.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0046, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Validates block-level enforcement of the pre-condition

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas cost computed BEFORE memory allocation in ModExp precompile?

reachability.notes: If memory is allocated before gas check, an attacker can trigger OOM by providing very large lengths with insufficient gas.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the ModExp precompile implementation and identify the entry point for CALL/STATICCALL/DELEGATECALL dispatch. 2. Trace the execution flow to verify the order of operations: (a) Parse base_length, exp_length, mod_length from input bytes 0-96. (b) Compute gas cost using EIP-2565 formula based on parsed lengths. (c) Check if available gas >= computed cost; if not, return OUT_OF_GAS without proceeding. (d) Only AFTER gas check passes, allocate memory buffers for base, exponent, modulus. (e) Read operand data into allocated buffers. 3. Craft a test transaction: CALL to ModExp (0x05) with calldata specifying extremely large lengths (e.g., base_length=2^30, exp_length=2^30, mod_length=2^30) but providing minimal gas (e.g., 21000 + small buffer). 4. Execute and verify: (a) Transaction reverts with OUT_OF_GAS, (b) No memory allocation occurred (check via memory profiling or debugger), (c) Node remains stable with no OOM conditions. 5. Compare memory usage before and after the failed call to confirm no allocation spike.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0047, Trust Boundary: tb-008, Primary Element: SG-003. PoC: Call ModExp with large lengths and minimal gas; show that no memory allocation occurs before gas rejection.

checklist.title: Verify EVM-to-Precompile dispatch enforces gas metering before resource allocation

reachability.notes: If memory is allocated before gas check, an attacker can trigger OOM by providing very large lengths with insufficient gas.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the precompile dispatch mechanism in the EVM implementation (typically a switch/match on address 0x01-0x09+). 2. For ModExp (0x05), verify the contract interface: (a) RequiredGas(input) is called FIRST to determine gas cost, (b) If RequiredGas > available_gas, execution halts immediately, (c) Run(input) is called ONLY after gas is deducted. 3. Review RequiredGas implementation: confirm it parses lengths from input WITHOUT allocating memory proportional to those lengths. 4. Review Run implementation: confirm memory allocation for operands happens at the START of Run(), not in RequiredGas(). 5. Test edge cases: (a) Empty input (lengths default to 0), (b) Truncated input (less than 96 bytes), (c) Maximum valid lengths that fit in available gas, (d) Lengths that overflow uint64 multiplication in gas calculation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0047, Supporting check for actor-evm and actor-modexp-precompile interaction. The dispatch pattern must ensure gas accounting precedes any expensive operations.

checklist.title: Verify ModExp gas calculation does not trigger memory allocation as a side effect

reachability.notes: If memory is allocated before gas check, an attacker can trigger OOM by providing very large lengths with insufficient gas.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Examine the gas calculation function (RequiredGas/GasModExp) for ModExp precompile. 2. Verify that the function: (a) Only reads the first 96 bytes of input to extract lengths, (b) Performs arithmetic operations to compute gas cost, (c) Does NOT create any buffers, slices, or allocations based on the parsed lengths. 3. Check for subtle allocation patterns: (a) No big.Int creation with SetBytes on length-sized data, (b) No slice operations like make([]byte, length), (c) No copying of input data beyond the length fields. 4. Static analysis: Search for allocation calls (make, new, append) within the gas calculation code path. 5. Dynamic analysis: Run gas calculation with absurdly large lengths and profile memory; allocation should be O(1) not O(length).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0047, Supporting check for actor-modexp-precompile. Even computing gas must not allocate attacker-controlled memory sizes.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7883 MODEXP gas formula correctly implemented for all specified test vectors?

reachability.notes: Concrete test vectors that all client implementations must agree on.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Execute MODEXP precompile with test vector 1: base_length=1, mod_length=1, exp_length=1, exp=2 and verify gas cost equals exactly 500. 2. Execute MODEXP precompile with test vector 2: base_length=64, mod_length=64, exp_length=64 with exp having bit_length=256 and verify gas cost equals exactly 98176. 3. Cross-validate results against multiple client implementations (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon) to detect consensus divergence. 4. Verify complexity calculation: for test 1, confirm complexity=16, iterations=1; for test 2, confirm complexity=128, iterations=767. 5. Verify floor() operation is applied correctly in the final gas calculation. 6. Test edge cases where max(500, calculated_gas) boundary is reached.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0048, Trust Boundaries: tb-007, tb-008. This is a post-condition verifying EIP-7883 formula correctness. Formula errors at these specific test vectors indicate implementation bugs that will cause chain splits between clients. The test vectors are: (1) Simple case returning minimum gas of 500; (2) Complex case with full 64-byte operands computing to gas=98176.

checklist.title: Verify MODEXP Precompile Gas Calculation Components: complexity, iterations, and floor operations

reachability.notes: Concrete test vectors that all client implementations must agree on.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify complexity calculation for base/mod length <= 64: complexity = (max(base_length, mod_length))^2 / 64. For test vector 1: complexity = ceil(1*1/64) = 16 (minimum complexity). For test vector 2: complexity = 64^2/64 = 64, then 2*64 = 128 (accounting for EIP-7883 adjustment). 2. Verify iterations calculation: iterations = 16 * (exp_length - 32) + (exp_bit_length - 1). For test vector 1: iterations = 1 (minimum). For test vector 2: iterations = 16*(64-32) + (256-1) = 512 + 255 = 767. 3. Verify final gas formula: gas = max(500, floor(complexity * iterations)). For test vector 1: max(500, 16*1) = 500. For test vector 2: max(500, 128*767) = max(500, 98176) = 98176. 4. Confirm integer arithmetic is used throughout (no floating point). 5. Test boundary conditions where exp_length equals 32 exactly.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0048, Supporting check for primary boundary check. Covers node: actor-modexp-precompile. This falsification check attempts to find discrepancies in the gas formula components that could lead to incorrect final values.
